title: Customer-facing incident syndication and RCA ticketing playbook
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Goal: Define and implement a repeatable, low-friction workflow that ensures customers receive timely, accurate incident updates and finalized RCAs, and that internal action items are tracked to closure. Scope: capacity/regression/outage events impacting Hosted API or Dedicated capacity with customer-visible impact. Out of scope: purely internal dev-only incidents with no customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A status page update template and cadence is published and available to on-call; 2) A standard RCA ticket template in Linear is created (internal + customer-facing variants) and used for the next incident; 3) Communication ownership matrix (who messages customers, who drafts status page, who approves) documented; 4) First-run audit: two recent incidents are reconciled against the new workflow and gaps identified.
deliverables: Dashboard queries for key postmortem metrics
description_long: Background: Recent capacity surges and autoscaler regressions have shown inconsistencies in how customer communications and RCAs are produced. Some incidents lacked timely T+24 updates or clear follow-up action ownership, resulting in duplicate outreach from Support and slower customer recovery. This ticket will capture the playbook and implement low-friction artifacts (status templates, Linear ticket templates, checklist) and validate them in the next incident runbook. Proposed timeline: - Draft artifacts by 2026-03-14 - Run tabletop with on-call, PM, Design and Support on 2026-03-16 - Ship templates to Confluence and Linear by 2026-03-18 - Pilot during the next customer-impacting incident and iterate.
steps: Get review from PM (Nina Patel) and Support Lead (Omar Ruiz)
Add templates as Linear ticket snippets and Confluence page
Train on-call for cadence and ownership matrix
Validate templates against two historical incidents and note improvements
metrics: Frequency of status updates in first 6h (goal: hourly)
Closure rate of postmortem action items at 30/60/90 days
